description: {"blocks":[{"key":"8kmm0","text":"This protocol describes hybridization capture of targeted genomic regions for Oxford nanopore-based sequencing starting with individually  PCR barcoded DNA (such as EXP-PCA001 or EXP-PBC001- PCR) sequencing libraries using SQK-LSK109 with customised xGen NGS discovery probes from Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT). Unlike some similar methodologies where placement of probes is tiled (1X or 2X) across the targeted regions, probes are minimally designed to conserved region to discover the diversity of targeted genes using our Probe Maker software. Briefly, the 5’ biotinylated 120-mer probes specific to conserved regions (regions with less than 7 polymorphic sites) of targeted gene are used with an interval of 700 to 1000 nt. Multiple barcoded samples (up to 65 samples) will be pooled prior to sequencing to minimize the cost and simplify the workflow. The hybrid capture is adapted from IDT xGen Hybridization and Wash kit protocol (with overnight hybridization) and sequencing library preparation and PCR barcoding steps are adapted from PCR barcoding (96) genomic DNA (SQK-LSK109) [version PBGE96_9068_v109_revN_14Aug2019]  . Streptavidin–coated magnetic beads are used to bind and extract biotinylated probe-hybridized target DNA. The duration of this protocol is  2 days.
